passages.original: Nec tamen æternum modico pro tempore quærat, 321 Et neget, Abraham tantum fecisse bea- [tum, Vel quoscunque docet sancta Scriptura fideles' Historias currant Danaum, gentisque Quirinæ. Qua pro laude sua, vel qua pro regno alieno, Mentibus infectis animosae cladis amore, Ausi omnes scelorare manus do morte suo- [rum, Aut certe de sirage sua. Menccea Creontis 322 Statius ostendit, qui fuso sponte cruore, Ut pater orbatus furiarum regna teneret, Thebanos proprio perfudit sanguine muros. i60 Si consanguineos scelus est jugulare propin- [ quos, Est furiale nefas in se convertere ferrum.
passages.english: Yet let him not seek [to deny] the eternal for a brief span of time, and deny that blessed Abraham did so much, or whatever faithful ones Holy Scripture teaches [of]; let him run through the histories of the Greeks and of the race of Quirinus. For their own glory, or for another's kingdom, their minds tainted with love of spirited slaughter, all dared to stain their hands with the death of their own kin, or indeed with their own destruction. Statius shows Menoeceus, son of Creon, who, shedding his blood of his own will so that his bereaved father might hold the kingdom of the Furies, drenched the walls of Thebes with his own blood. If it is a crime to cut the throats of kinsmen related by blood, it is a monstrous wickedness to turn the sword upon oneself.
passages.notes: Scanning errors silently corrected: 'scelorare' read as 'scelerare', 'do morte' as 'de morte', 'sirage' as 'strage', 'Menccea' as 'Menoecea' (Menoeceus). The numbers 321, 322 and 'i60' are edition line/column markers and have been omitted. The first line is elliptical: 'quærat' (seek) and 'neget' (deny) are paired, and the sense of 'seek the eternal for a brief time' is uncertain; it may mean 'let him not question the eternal on the basis of a brief time'. 'regna furiarum' (kingdom of the Furies) presumably refers to the cursed throne of Thebes. 'animosae cladis' rendered 'spirited slaughter'; the text may be corrupt here.
